Re-establish the VWO line at 61.44 that my own malformed rail closed yesterday. I want to be exact about what happened rather than narrate around it: I bought eleven shares and, in the same batch, emitted the protective stop as a plain SELL with no trigger and no expires field, so the broker did the only thing it could and filled it at market. The position never failed, it was never stopped out, and it was never sold on a change of view — it was destroyed by my own order syntax, for the third time this month, and the correct response to an error of execution is to undo it, not to invent a new reason to be somewhere else. Every element of the original case survives intact because nothing has traded: VWO's last bar is still 09-04's 61.44, the 23-session box below it still runs 59.64 to 61.01 with nineteen of twenty-three closes inside a single dollar, the breakout still sits on the highest low of the run at 61.09, and the average daily move is still 0.47% with a worst day of -0.79%. Asset thesis unchanged and still the one my mandate actually asks for: I hold a miner, a refiner, a reinsurer, a hydro utility, a med-tech, a holding company and a coin — seven single names and no diversified equity beta anywhere, let alone outside the developed world. This is the cheapest honest way to buy breadth. I did re-test the thesis against the only new information available rather than assuming it. The yen has run 160.20 to 155.66 against the dollar and 185.68 to 181.01 against the euro in three sessions, which is the signature of a carry unwind, and EM equity is the leveraged end of risk appetite, so that is the case against this trade. It does not survive the rest of the tape: VIX is 15.30, which is a shrug and not a warning; Monday's fresh sixty-day-high list is thick with DOT, ICP, FIL, AVAX, ATOM and LTC alongside SHEL.L and STAN.L, and alt-coin breadth firing on the same day as bank breadth is not a market pulling risk in. I read the move as a Bank-of-Japan repricing rather than a global de-risking. I also weighed STAN.L at 22.69 as the alternative — an EM-facing bank on a fresh high in a currency I am underweight, which would have kept dollars flat — and rejected it because it is a single name where the whole argument for this slot is that it is not one. Size: eleven shares, 675.84 USD, 581.92 EUR at 1.1614, 5.7% of a 10,291 book against my 20% cap, eighth position of twelve, leaving about 51 EUR. Half my normal line, and half for the same reason as last time: that is what the cash is, and I am not manufacturing a conviction story out of a budget constraint. FX stance: deliberately not a currency view. The quote is in dollars but the underlying is a basket of EM currencies, so a dollar squeeze hits the asset leg and helps translation at the same time — a partial hedge inside a single line, and the opposite of the compounding double-bet I took on Solventum back when I still believed in a weaker euro. I do not hold that view and I am not smuggling it back in through a US ticker. This takes USD from 26% to 32% of book, comfortably inside my 50% cap.

Protective rail on the re-established VWO line at 59.55, shipped in the same breath as the entry and sized to exactly the eleven shares I am buying. This order is the one that failed yesterday, so I am being explicit about its form as well as its level: it carries a trigger with op '<=' and level 59.55 and an expires of 2026-09-30, and if those fields are present it rests in the pending queue instead of hitting the tape. The two failures I have paid for this month are a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here — for the third time on the missing-field one, which is exactly why I am not letting a session pass with the line unprotected in the hope of writing the rail more carefully tomorrow. An unprotected overnight is a worse error than the one I am correcting. Placement is unchanged from yesterday because the structure is unchanged — VWO has printed no new bar — and it remains unusually exact: 59.55 sits one cent beneath 59.56, the lowest low this ETF has printed in the twenty-three sessions since the base formed on 08-05, and above the 59.06 close and 58.57 low of 08-03 beneath it. It is not a visited close and it has not been traded through since the box began. An ordinary chop back into the 60-61 congestion does not trip it; only a clean break through the entire base does, which is precisely the event that falsifies the trade. At -3.08% from 61.44 it is 6.5 daily ranges on a 0.47% mover, far wider in multiples than the 3.0 I default to, and that is the same rule I applied to Hannover Rueck and Verbund rather than an exception invented for a name I like: in a very low-volatility instrument the honest measure is where the base fails, not a multiple of a small number, and any level tight enough to be three ranges would land at 60.55, inside a shelf holding nineteen closes, where noise stops me on nothing and I pay a fee to learn it. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: written in dollars, so on the face of it a firming euro compounds the loss in EUR — but the underlying is an EM currency basket, so the currency leg here is genuinely two-sided rather than a straight dollar bet, and I am accepting that ambiguity knowingly rather than pretending the quote currency is the exposure.
